chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr; and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Ali (peace be upon him), when he seized two men in one quilt, would flog them both with the hadd (prescribed penalty); and when he seized two women in one quilt, he would flog them both with the hadd.

key_terms.الحد: Hadd — a prescribed punishment stipulated in the Quran or sunnah for specific offenses
key_terms.اللحاف: Quilt/blanket; the shared covering is the circumstantial evidence triggering the ruling
key_terms.ضرب الحد: Inflicting the hadd lashing — the act of carrying out the prescribed penalty

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on two men or two women found under one cover?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reports that Imam Ali (AS) applied the hadd (prescribed lashing) to both two men or two women found sharing a single quilt. This ruling reflects the jurisprudential principle in Shia fiqh that physical seclusion or proximity suggestive of illicit conduct between persons of the same sex is subject to a ta'zir or hadd penalty at the judge's discretion. The historical audience—early Shia jurists—would have understood this as evidence of Imam Ali's strict implementation of Islamic penal law even in circumstances short of proven zina.
